instrument_name: MCA 39-3-204 Payment of wages generally
figure_or_rule_carried: Wages in lawful money or checks convertible at face value; may not withhold wages more than 10 business days after due; reasonable deductions for board, room, incidentals; direct deposit/EFT only with employee written or electronic consent (record retained), employee may not be required to use it; late timesheet -> next ensuing pay period; no established pay period -> presumed semimonthly. History amd. Ch. 26 L. 2009 (effective date of amendment not printed; 2009-10-01 = MT default effective date, inferred).

instrument_name: MCA 39-3-205 Payment of wages when employee separated prior to payday
figure_or_rule_carried: Separation (quit): all unpaid wages due next regular payday for the period of separation or 15 days from separation, whichever first. Separated for cause or laid off: due immediately unless written personnel policy extends to next regular payday or within 15 days, whichever first. Theft allegation: withhold value with written consent, or police report within 7 business days (no charges in 30 days -> due).

instrument_name: MCA 39-3-405 Overtime compensation
figure_or_rule_carried: Overtime 1.5x hourly rate over 40 hours/workweek; not for farm workers; seasonal amusement/recreation students furnished board/lodging: 1.5x over 48 hours; state firefighters/law enforcement consistent with FLSA. No daily overtime.

instrument_name: MCA 39-3-409 Adoption of minimum wage rates (I.M. 151, 2006)
figure_or_rule_carried: Minimum wage = greater of FLSA 206(a)(1) rate or 6.15/h, excluding tips (no tip credit) and training wage; adjusted by 30 September each year by CPI-U U.S. city average all items, August to August; rounded to nearest 5 cents; effective 1 January following. Business with annual gross sales 110,000 or less: 4.00/h.

instrument_name: Montana Employer and Information Agent Guide V4 November 2025: payment schedule, MW-3/W-2 filing, records, POA, filing options
article_or_section: pp. 2-8 (Exemptions; Payment Schedule and Lookback Period; Annual Filing; Penalties; Recordkeeping; TAP; Filing Options)
figure_or_rule_carried: Lookback 1 July-30 June: >=12,000 accelerated (federal schedule); 1,200-11,999 monthly by 15th of following month; <=1,199 annual by 31 January; MW-1 voucher for mail; MW-3 + all W-2s due 31 January (federal W-3 not accepted; truncated SSNs not accepted); upload in EFW2 or Pub 1220 via TAP File Processing Account; MW-4 exemption claims submitted via TAP by last day of payroll period, renewed by 31 January; final MW-3/W-2 within 30 days of ceasing; late payment 1.5%/month max 15%; W-2 late filing 50 per form min 250; interest 10.25%/yr; records 5 years (ARM 42.17.203); POA Form POA or federal 2848. Exempt from withholding without MW-4: agricultural laborers, interstate motor/rail carrier nonresidents, active-duty armed forces; with MW-4: tribal members on own reservation, MT National Guard Title 10, ND residents, military spouses; H-2A exempt; NRA treaty exclusion not applied at withholding.

instrument_name: MCA 39-3-406 Exclusions from minimum wage and overtime
figure_or_rule_carried: (1) Min wage + OT exclusions incl. distributive-education students, babysitting/menial household chores, household child care hired by head of household, immediate family/dependents, apprentices/learners up to 30 days (commissioner), farm learners under 18 up to 180 days at >=50% of minimum, EAP and outside sales, computer employees >=27.63/h, US federal employees, resident managers of lodging/assisted living, direct sellers (26 USC 3508), companionship in domestic service employed by family, seasonal nonprofit camps, postsecondary student housing assistants. (2) OT-only exclusions incl. motor carrier (49 USC 31502), agriculture, taxi drivers, licensed-outfitter guides, retail commission (>1.5x FLSA minimum and >half commissions), hospital 8/80 work period (OT over 8/day or 80/14 days), municipal/county 40-hour 7-day period, firefighter/police work periods.

instrument_name: MCA 39-51-1108 Amount of wages per employee subject to contribution
figure_or_rule_carried: UI taxable wage base each year = greater of 80% of average annual wage under 39-51-2201 (rounded to nearest 100) for the calendar year immediately preceding the most recently completed year, or the FUTA base. Mechanism behind 2026 base 47,300 (US-MT-P5-1-005).

instrument_name: MCA 49-2-310 Maternity leave -- unlawful acts of employers (Montana Maternity Leave Act)
figure_or_rule_carried: Unlawful to terminate for pregnancy, refuse reasonable leave of absence for pregnancy, deny disability/leave benefits accrued under employer plans to employee disabled by pregnancy, or force unreasonably long mandatory leave. Covers all employers (no size threshold in section); leave unpaid by statute.

instrument_name: MCA 25-13-614 Earnings of judgment debtor
figure_or_rule_carried: Garnishment limit = lesser of disposable weekly earnings above 30x federal minimum hourly wage or 25% of disposable earnings (mirrors CCPA). Support orders: 50% (supporting other spouse/child) / 60%, +5 points (55/65%) for arrears older than 12 weeks. Definitions per 15 USC 1672.

instrument_name: MCA 18-2-401 Prevailing wage definitions (public works contract threshold)
figure_or_rule_carried: Public works contract = construction services let by state/county/municipality/school district/political subdivision, or nonconstruction services (maintenance, custodial, security, food service, transport driving etc.) let by state/county/municipality/political subdivision, total cost in excess of 25,000; prevailing rates per 18-2-413/-414/-415; fringe benefits ERISA-qualified. Confirms US-MT-P5-1-007 threshold from primary text.

instrument_name: MCA 18-2-423 Submission of payroll records (prevailing wage)
figure_or_rule_carried: On complaint, department may require certified copies of payroll records for the project; contractors/subcontractors on public works must pay hourly employees WEEKLY; payroll records to department within 5 days of request.

instrument_name: MCA 40-5-922 Directory of new hires -- employer reporting requirements
figure_or_rule_carried: Report hire or rehire to DPHHS (CSED) by copy of W-4 or equivalent: employee name, date of hire, SSN, residential and mailing addresses; employer name, address, FEIN; optional DOB and dependent health coverage availability. Within 20 days of hire/rehire; electronic: two monthly transmissions 12-16 days apart; multistate electronic employers may designate one state (notice to HHS). Section marked (Temporary), terminates on contingency (sec. 1 Ch. 27 L. 1999).

instrument_name: MCA 40-5-415 and 40-5-416 Child support administrative income withholding
figure_or_rule_carried: Order binding on service; payor withholds monthly amount and delivers to the department in the SAME MONTH withheld; arrears add greater of 2-year payoff or 25% of income; payor fee up to 5 USD per month if allowed by department; may annualize to weekly/biweekly; total incl. fees capped at CCPA 15 USC 1673(b).

instrument_name: Montana DLI 2026 Minimum Wage poster (Effective 1/1/2026)
authority: Montana Department of Labor and Industry, Employment Relations Division
figure_or_rule_carried: Montana minimum wage 10.85/h effective 2026-01-01; non-FLSA business with gross annual sales 110,000 or less may pay 4.00/h (FLSA-covered individual employees get the greater rate); OT 1.5x over 40/workweek; pay within 10 business days after end of pay period; quit: next scheduled payday or 15 calendar days whichever first; laid off/discharged: immediately (within four hours or end of business day, whichever first) unless written policy; NO tip credit, training wage or meal credit. Derivation check: 10.55 x (1+2.92%) = 10.86 -> 10.85 (US-MTS5-016).

instrument_name: Montana DLI 2025 Minimum Wage Determination Letter (method of calculation)
authority: Montana Department of Labor and Industry
figure_or_rule_carried: 2025 minimum wage 10.55 (from 10.30): CPI-U increase over prior year 2.53%, inflation adjustment 0.26, subtotal 10.56, rounded to nearest 0.05 = 10.55. Establishes the department's method: current ROUNDED rate x CPI-U Aug/Aug % (2 decimals), adjustment to cents, then nearest 0.05.

instrument_name: BLS CPI-U U.S. city average, all items, NSA (series CUUR0000SA0), August values
figure_or_rule_carried: CPI-U Aug 2024 314.796; Aug 2025 323.976; Aug 2026 334.980. Caliber per MCA 39-3-409(2)(b): U.S. city average, all urban consumers, all items (NSA). 2026 derivation: 323.976/314.796 = +2.92%; 10.55 x 2.92% = 0.31; 10.86 -> 10.85 = published 2026 rate (US-MTS5-014). 2027 derivation (same method): 334.980/323.976 = +3.40%; 10.85 x 3.40% = 0.37; 11.22 -> 11.20 (published 2027 letter not obtained).

instrument_name: Montana minimum wage 2027 (derived; DLI 2027 Determination Letter not obtained)
authority: Montana Department of Labor and Industry (letter expected by 2026-09-30)
figure_or_rule_carried: DERIVED, NOT PUBLISHED-READ: 11.20/h from 2027-01-01 (10.85 x (1+3.40%) = 11.22 -> 11.20). Must be confirmed against the DLI 2027 letter/poster before WTC consumption.

instrument_name: MT DLI Office of Administrative Hearings, Herden v. Black Smoke Diesel Performance LLC, Case No. 1184-2020 (Final Agency Decision) applying Langager v. Crazy Creek Prods., 1998 MT 44
authority: Montana Department of Labor and Industry, Office of Administrative Hearings
figure_or_rule_carried: Earned and due vacation pay is wages (39-3-201(6)), collectible as wages: 23 Op. Att'y Gen. 151 (1949); Langager v. Crazy Creek Prods., 1998 MT 44, 287 Mont. 445, 954 P.2d 1169 (in force; operates at final pay / wage claim level). Once accrued under the employer's policy, employer may not impose conditions subsequent that divest it (use-it-or-lose-it forfeiture of accrued vacation not enforceable); accrual terms (conditions precedent) set by employer. Penalty on unpaid wages 55% under ARM 24.16.7566 (rule not read directly).

instrument_name: MCA 39-3-201 Definitions (wages) and 39-3-206 penalty
figure_or_rule_carried: Wages = any money due from employer by hour/day/week/semimonth/month/year incl. bonus, piecework, tips and gratuities (IRC 3402(k)) and service charges for food/beverage/lodging premises; service charge must be distributed to nonmanagement serving staff per tip pool. Employer excludes the United States. Failure to pay per part 2: misdemeanor + penalty up to 110% of wages due and unpaid.

instrument_name: MCA 30-14-1703 Record destruction and 30-14-1704 Computer security breach (Impediment of Identity Theft)
figure_or_rule_carried: Business must destroy customer records with personal information no longer needed (shred/erase). Breach of computerized personal information (name + SSN, DL/tribal ID, financial account, medical, TIN, IRS IP PIN) -> notify Montana residents without unreasonable delay; copy to Attorney General consumer protection office. No Montana provision requiring SSN truncation on pay statements located; DOR requires FULL SSN on W-2/1099 filed with MW-3 (US-MTS5-005).

instrument_name: MCA 39-51-204 Exclusions from definition of employment (UI)
figure_or_rule_carried: UI excludes: domestic service in private home (unless 39-51-202(3) monetary test met), dependent child/spouse of sole proprietor, freelance correspondents/newspaper carriers with written acknowledgment, commission-only real estate/insurance agents, qualifying booth-rent cosmetologists/barbers, casual labor (<300 or not regularly employed), floor installers under contract, direct sellers, petroleum land professionals, agricultural labor (unless 39-51-202 tests met), other-state/federal government, students employed by their school, co-op students, vessel crew, aliens F, H-2A, J, M, Q, companionship/respite care hired by family, amateur sports officials, AmeriCorps/VISTA. For 501(c)(3)/government (39-51-203(5),(6)): ministers and religious order members, sheltered workshop, work relief, inmates, community service, elected officials, election judges <1,000/yr. (4) Exclusions do not apply to government/tribes/501(c)(3) unless excluded under FUTA.

instrument_name: MCA 15-30-2103 Rate of tax (temporary through 2026-12-31 and version effective 2027-01-01, HB 337 = Ch. 227 L. 2025)
figure_or_rule_carried: TY2026: 4.7% to 95,000 joint/surviving spouse, 71,250 HoH, 47,500 single and MFS; 5.65% above (terminates 2026-12-31, sec. 7 Ch. 227 L. 2025). TY2027: 4.7% to 130,000 joint, 97,500 HoH, 65,000 single/MFS; 5.4% above; brackets indexed by 1 November each year by modified inflation factor with CPI June 2026 as base (so 2027 factor = 1.0 and 2027 brackets are the statutory figures; first indexation applies to TY2028). Capital gains 3.0%/4.1%. Reconciles guide annual table: 16,100 (federal std deduction single) + 47,500 = 63,600 (US-MT-P5-1-001).

instrument_name: MCA 39-51-1103 Contributions by employers; 39-51-201(25) definition of wages (UI)
figure_or_rule_carried: Contributions accrue per calendar year on wages paid; due per department rules (ARM, not read) and may not be deducted from wages; fractions of a cent: half cent or more rounds up to 1 cent; 501(c)(3), state/political subdivisions and tribes may elect reimbursement. UI wages include commissions, bonuses, OT, holiday/vacation/sick pay, severance, backpay, reported tips, cash value of non-cash remuneration; EXCLUDE employer payments for qualified retirement plans, workers' comp disability, medical/hospitalization incl. employee/family health insurance, life insurance, expense reimbursements per rule, no-additional-cost services, owner draws (39-51-207). No out-of-state wage-base credit language in 39-51-1108 or 39-51-201.

authority: Montana Department of Labor and Industry, UI Division

instrument_name: Montana DLI UI Division Employer Handbook (Revised January 2025; PDF modified 2026-03-04)
authority: Montana Department of Labor and Industry, Unemployment Insurance Division
article_or_section: Sections 2-6 (special classes table pp. 5-8; multistate test p. 9; excess wages p. 14; payments and reports p. 16; penalties p. 17)
figure_or_rule_carried: Quarterly UI wage report + payment due Apr 30 / Jul 31 / Oct 31 / Jan 31 (next business day if weekend/holiday); ALL quarterly UI reports must be filed electronically from 2025-07-01 per ARM 24.40.1609 (UI eServices for Employers; E-Filing Handbook); electronic payment optional. Late report 25 flat; interest 1.5%/month (18%/yr); non-electronic filing may draw 25 fee. Wages reported to OTHER states may NOT be used to reach the Montana wage base (only MT-reported wages count). UI taxable: Section 125 cafeteria salary reductions; 401(k) and other elective deferrals; Section 129 dependent care; corporate officer pay (incl. S corp); personal use of company vehicle; vacation, holiday, severance pay; tips documented and allocated; room and board at cash value, minimum 130/week full board, 3/meal; 3rd-party sick pay first 6 months when employer paid premiums. Exempt: employer qualified-plan contributions, employer health/life premiums, ministers/religious orders, F/H-2A/J/M/Q aliens, students of own school (12 undergrad/9 grad credits), director fees. Household: covered if cash wages 1,000+ in any quarter; agricultural: 20,000 in a quarter or 10 workers on 20 days in 20 weeks. Four-part localization test for multistate workers.
